All coords zero-based.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T04:19:13.612879+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T04:19:13.612891+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_draw_bounding_box_perimeter_around_marker_set', kind='memory', title='ARC: draw bounding-box perimeter around marker set', content='For ARC grids with a uniform background and scattered same-color marker cells (seen with marker colors 3/4 and other backgrounds), find the minimum axis-aligned bounding rectangle containing all markers. Recolor every non-marker cell along the rectangle perimeter with color 2; preserve the original markers and leave all interior/exterior cells unchanged. Demonstrations: demo 1 markers were on the outer edges of the bbox rows 0,7 and cols 2,10; gaps on those four edges became 2. Demo 2 bbox rows 2..9, cols 4..8; output completed the rectangle perimeter with 2. A prior hypothesis to connect all collinear markers throughout the grid was wrong; do not fill interior columns/rows. Test task-666ceaba solved with bbox rows 6..22, cols 0..7.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T02:43:48.857011+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T02:43:48.857022+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_fill_gaps_in_broken_aligned_rectangular_rails', kind='memory', title='ARC: Fill gaps in broken aligned rectangular rails', content='For ARC grids with a uniform background and a single non-background color forming incomplete axis-aligned rectangular frame(s), fill missing cells along the frame rails with a new color (demo examples used 2), preserving original pixels and background. The rails may include intermediate horizontal dividers, not only the outermost rectangle: infer full straight rows/columns from existing aligned segments and connected frame structure, then place the repair color in gaps on those rails. Example task-666ceaba: background 4, frame color 3 with rails at rows 2, 4, 8 and columns 0, 5; missing cells on those rails become 2. A first guess that completed only the outer frame missed row 4, c1; the correct result also filled this mid-divider gap. Demonstrations showed the same rule with background 9/frame 5 and background 7/frame 0, repair color 2. Do not recolor interior/off-rail noise.', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T01:57:12.796201+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T01:57:12.796214+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_fill_spans_between_same_color_markers_in_rows_and_columns', kind='memory', title='ARC: fill spans between same-color markers in rows and columns', content='For sparse ARC grids with a uniform background and isolated pixels of one marker color, inspect demos for the rule: for every row containing at least two marker pixels, recolor background cells from the leftmost through rightmost marker with 3; for every column containing at least two markers, recolor background cells from the topmost through bottommost marker with 3. Preserve original marker cells and all background cells outside those horizontal/vertical spans. The row and column spans combine by union. Demonstrated with marker colors 1 or 5, background 2, output fill 3; also works with marker 0/background 9. Check demos for differing output fill color if needed.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T01:29:08.899257+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T01:29:08.899271+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_rule_overlap_aligned_panels_into_color_2', kind='memory', title='ARC rule: overlap aligned panels into color 2', content='For ARC grids split into two equal-sized panels by a uniform one-cell divider row or column, compare aligned cells across panels. Output a grid the size of one panel, with color 2 wherever both corresponding input cells are nonzero, and 0 elsewhere. Ignore the divider and original foreground colors. This applies whether either panel is sparse or dense; it was demonstrated across horizontal and vertical splits. Practical check: for a vertical split, align each left-panel column with the same-index right-panel column; for a horizontal split, align rows. Ensure every overlap is included (a missed single overlap caused one wrong submission on task-b4c2378b).', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T02:23:32.849121+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T02:23:32.849131+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_noisy_rectangles_restore_filled_blocks_and_remove_speckles', kind='memory', title='ARC noisy rectangles: restore filled blocks and remove speckles', content='For ARC-style grids with a uniform background and several solid, axis-aligned monochrome rectangular objects corrupted by single-cell color substitutions, restore each object to its solid rectangle color and replace unrelated stray pixels with the background. Infer each true rectangle from the consistent filled rectangular footprint, not just 4-connected same-color components: noisy cells inside a rectangle can have arbitrary colors (including background, zero, or other object colors). Preserve full rectangles, including small 2x2 blocks; clean isolated noise outside rectangles back to background. Examples: backgrounds 9/3 with valid rectangles of 0,3,6,7,8; singleton contaminants inside blocks are recolored to the block color, while isolated contaminants elsewhere become background. Be careful to infer exact rectangle bounds: do not extend a rectangle for a protruding singleton or truncate rows that are part of the filled rectangle. This task family may have many disconnected rectangles and multiple colors.', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T04:54:45.716309+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T04:54:45.716325+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_sparse_markers_receive_centered_exemplar_stamps', kind='memory', title='ARC sparse markers receive centered exemplar stamps', content='Continual-ARC pattern: A mostly uniform grid contains many isolated marker cells of one color and a separate exemplar/template patch made from non-background colors (possibly including background-colored cells). Output copies the exemplar centered on every marker: align the exemplar center cell with the marker, overwrite the marker with the exemplar center color, and paint the exemplar’s non-background cells at the same relative offsets. Keep all other background cells unchanged. The exemplar itself is left intact. Evidence: two demos. Demo 1 background 9, markers 6, exemplar vertical [7,5,5]; each 6 became a 3-cell vertical stamp with 7 above and 5 at/under the marker. Demo 2 background 0, markers 3, exemplar [9,6,6]; each 3 became 9 above, 6 at/under. Test background 5 had a 3x3 exemplar [[3,6,1],[9,3,7],[6,5,5]] in the top-left and 0 markers; centered copies solved correctly. Exemplar’s background-colored cells simply blend into the field.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T03:25:46.307439+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T03:25:46.307451+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_sparse_rectangle_border_completion_with_color_2', kind='memory', title='ARC sparse rectangle border completion with color 2', content='For ARC grids with a uniform background and sparse pixels of a single marker color, examples show completing a rectangular outline in color 2 while preserving marker pixels. Use the min/max row and column extents of the marker set as the outer rectangle; color 2 fills any missing cells along its four edges, even if a corner marker is absent on one edge. Also fill gaps between marker-color cells along any common row/column containing at least 3 marker pixels (e.g. an interior row with several scattered marks); do not bridge a mere pair in an interior row/column. Existing marker pixels remain unchanged; all other cells stay background. Validation examples: complete-border rectangles need no edits; sparse marker points on two side columns and top/bottom edges get 2s on missing edge segments; a scattered interior row with >=3 marks is connected with 2. In one test, the bounding rectangle perimeter plus a heavily populated interior row was correct, while global line-connection of every pair and bounding-box-only were both wrong. Color/background may vary (demos included 0 background/4 markers, 9 background/0 or 8 markers; output fill 2). Treat exact threshold/conditions cautiously, but the above behavior fit multiple demonstrations and a solved test.', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T03:23:40.060924+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T03:23:40.060936+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_rule_intersect_paired_panels_into_color_2', kind='memory', title='ARC: intersect nonzero cells across aligned panels', content='For two same-sized panels separated by a uniform row/column, align corresponding cells directly and output panel-sized grid with 2 where both aligned input cells are nonzero, else 0; ignore divider and original colors. For task-b4c2378b specifically, nonzero—not the sparse/zero cells—is the foreground criterion. Demo: upper mostly 8 with zero holes, lower mostly 0 with 7 marks; output exactly where upper=8 and lower=7. Test: upper mostly 1 and lower mostly 9, each with zero holes; output 2 wherever neither aligned cell is zero. Treat this as a nonzero-cell intersection, not a same-color match or an intersection of zero locations.', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T02:15:05.128355+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T04:15:03.000421+00:00', version=2)]
